label: rem:explicit-alpha-k-h4-proof-sketch
title: Proof sketch: explicit alpha k h4
html:
Proof sketch

By α_k derivation procedure, the depth-k stratum coefficient \alpha_k(H_n) is the Markov pairing of \mathrm{tr}_M with a class-function representative r_k that is Wedderburn-orthogonal to every lower-depth irrep — i.e. \chi_\lambda(r_k) = 0 for every \lambda \,\vdash\, n with \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) < k.

The class-function basis. The natural basis for class functions on H_n is the set of canonical conjugacy-class representatives \{T_{w_C}\}_C. At H_4 this is 5-dimensional. The length-restricted (length-k word) approach fails: at H_4 the 6 length-3 reduced words collapse to just 2 conjugacy classes (3-cycle + 4-cycle) — only a 2-dim space, insufficient to satisfy 4 lower-depth orthogonality constraints.

Linear system. Let M \in \mathbb{R}^{4 \times 5} have entries M_{i, C} = \chi_{\lambda_i}(T_{w_C}) for the four lower-depth partitions \lambda \in \{(4), (3, 1), (2, 2), (2, 1, 1)\} indexed by i, and the five conjugacy classes C. The system

  M \cdot \mathbf{c} \;=\; \mathbf{0},
  \qquad \mathbf{c} \in \mathbb{R}^5,

has a 1-dimensional solution space at generic q (the Hoefsmit character matrix is full row-rank since the irreps are distinct). Fixing the gauge c_{C_4} = 1, the remaining coefficients are uniquely determined.

canonical evaluation at q_0. Hoefsmit characters computed via seminormal matrices (see the formal derivation); the 5 \times 5 character matrix at q_0 is computed numerically.

Sanity verification — central character identity at every class:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{w_C})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \,\vdash\, 4} y_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(T_{w_C})

verifies to \sim 10^{-17} canonical precision against the Jones-Markov witness (y-lambda witness). This anchors the Hoefsmit character values.

Solving the system. \mathbf{c} = (-0.3056, +1.4541, -0.6127, -1.5593, +1.0000).

Exact check of the table. The numerical solve above fixes only the (1^4) row at q_0. The statement's table is exact: computing the five Hoefsmit characters on the class representatives e, T_{s_1}, T_{s_1 s_3}, T_{s_1 s_2}, T_{s_1 s_2 s_3} symbolically over \mathbb{Q}(q), every row r_\lambda of the table satisfies \chi_\mu(r_\lambda) = 0 for all \mu \ne \lambda and \chi_\lambda(r_\lambda) \ne 0, as identities of rational functions in q. So the five rows are the basis of class functions dual to the irreducible characters, normalised by c_{(1234)} = 1 (for (2,2), where c_{(1234)} = 0, by c_{(123)} = 1). The (1^4) row is the r_3 of this proof; at q_0 it reproduces the numerical solution.

Markov pairing on r_3. Markov-trace values on the 5 class representatives are universal (Markov reduction): \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{w_C}) \in \{1, z, z^2, z^2, z^3\} for the five classes respectively. Hence

  \mathrm{tr}_M(r_3)
  \;=\;
  c_0 + c_1 z + c_2 z^2 + c_3 z^2 + c_4 z^3
  \;\approx\; +0.003463.

By the central character expansion plus orthogonality,

  \mathrm{tr}_M(r_3)
  \;=\; \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi_\lambda(r_3)
  \;=\; y_{(1^4)} \cdot \chi_{(1^4)}(r_3)

(only the depth-3 term survives). Both sides agree to canonical precision, confirming the construction. \square
